Write a set of tables as Parquet with a manifest, and upload them

Source: R/publish.R
knw_publish.Rd

scripts/0299's pattern as a function: each table is written as zstd Parquet, compared column by column with an all-character read of its CSV (numbers within 1e-12, zero-padded codes kept as text, an empty or "NA" cell null on both sides), and described in a manifest.json that carries each file's rows, columns, bytes, sha256 and schema, the source CSV's sha256 and modification time, and the commit the set was published from. The bucket does not list, so a reader starts from the manifest.

Usage

knw_publish(
  tables,
  dir_out,
  id,
  note,
  provenance = list(),
  supersedes = NULL,
  s3 = NULL,
  republish = FALSE,
  no_sign = FALSE,
  hive = NULL,
  hive_keys = c("species_code", "stage")
)

Arguments

tables

data.frame with table, source (CSV path), script and description.

dir_out

character(1) where the Parquet and manifest are written.

id

character(1) the dataset id, e.g. "knowledge/thresholds/v1".

note

character(1) a sentence on what this version is.

provenance

a named list carried into the manifest (the link run, the evidence version, the commit).

supersedes

character(1) or NULL the id this version replaces.

s3

NULL, or the s3://bucket/ the id is published under.

republish

logical(1) allow replacing a published version's contents.

no_sign

logical(1) read the published manifest without credentials.

hive

NULL, or a character of table names whose Parquet is written under a Hive path <table>/<key>=<value>/part.parquet from the columns hive_keys (one part per distinct key combination).

hive_keys

character the Hive key columns.

Value

The manifest, invisibly.

Details

With s3 = NULL nothing is uploaded. With an s3:// prefix the published manifest is read first: a published version with different tables or schemas refuses (a change of columns or meaning is a new version), and one with the same tables but different contents refuses unless republish = TRUE. Parquet is uploaded before the manifest, so a reader never finds a manifest naming a file not yet there.

Examples

tmp <- tempfile()
dir.create(tmp)
csv <- file.path(tmp, "t.csv")
utils::write.csv(data.frame(a = 1:3, code = c("08", "09", "10")), csv, row.names = FALSE)
tables <- data.frame(table = "t", source = csv, script = "example", description = "three rows")
m <- knw_publish(tables, file.path(tmp, "out"), id = "example/v1", note = "an example",
                 provenance = list(commit = "none"))
m$files[[1]]$rows
#> [1] 3
